## Overview

A look at how a global pandemic-preparedness network's private-sector partnership strategy took shape over two terms — moving from stakeholder-facing strategy work to an independent spatial extension of it.

## Winter 2026 — Stakeholder Strategy

The engagement began as a capstone project for a health-forecasting network connecting regional health data across dozens of countries for pandemic preparedness. Through a round of stakeholder interviews, the work mapped the organization's private-sector landscape and used a five forces framework to identify where partnership value was most likely to materialize — landing on pharma, development finance, and tech/AI as the priority categories.

## Spring 2026 — Spatial Extension

The natural follow-on question was *where*, not just *who*. I took the five forces findings and built an independent GIS-driven prioritization framework, scoring candidate countries on digital health ecosystem maturity, CSR landscape, regulatory environment, and infrastructure readiness — turning a qualitative targeting list into a spatial one that could rank markets side by side.

## Takeaway

The sequence — stakeholder research first, spatial analysis second — is a pattern I keep coming back to: qualitative fieldwork tells you *who matters*, and GIS tells you *where to act on it*.

:::
